nodes.label: B-087: Baseline Alignment and Parent-First Planning Packet
nodes.description: Lane B finding that became the planning-spike record for baseline alignment. Read the entry header for current lifecycle status. It separates the original usable-by-Sprint-2 milestone from today's setup completion, and records the Judge's J1-J4 acts: J1 accepts 'setup/scaffold evidence' as a descriptive classification with no V0 release or rename; J2 (journey examples) and J3 (capacity) are deferred to the Chief Editor with named triggers; J4 Choice A keeps the iteration planning-only and defers B-084's governed-source application to its own Phase 1 unit. Two transferable rules: a planning record closes on accepted decisions plus a truthful disposition of every routed branch, not on completion of those branches; and graph currency needs four separate proofs - head equality with the final committed HEAD, document coverage, descriptions present and curated parity. J1-J4 are recorded in this entry only, by explicit choice, so a reader of the Register alone will not see them.
nodes.rationale: graph-coverage requires a curated node per docs/ markdown file. This node also carries the J1-J4 acts and the planning-versus-execution closure rule, which are otherwise reachable only by reading the full entry and the four reviews that corrected it.

nodes.label: B-088: C-39 Actor Guard Accepts Underscore-Suffixed Identifiers
nodes.description: Lane B failed-verification finding against the C-39 leading-actor guard. Read the entry header for current lifecycle status. The nine live positive and six negative actor examples reproduce, but an unknown identifier continued with an underscore (for example 'Lane B_fake') is accepted as its allowlisted prefix, because the suffix test excludes only letters and digits. The fix is token termination, not a larger allowlist. Guard repair alone cannot close C-39: audit-field and real-commit validation across every lifecycle position remains owed under D-214/D-215, and C-35 keeps its fixture prerequisite. It is a sibling of B-087 on an independent track and does not gate product alignment.
nodes.rationale: graph-coverage requires a curated node per docs/ markdown file. This node also records that a healthy live corpus cannot prove rejection of an unknown actor, and that the C-39 track is independent of B-087.

nodes.label: B-089: Independent Review of Lane A's B-087 Answer
nodes.description: Lane B review of Lane A's first B-087 answer. Read the entry header for current lifecycle status. It found that the CR-14 inventory omitted the highest-tier anchor, Modular_PRD section 7.1, which lists CR-14 as a missing functional requirement while FR-01 and the traceability map record the ratified manual contract - a contradiction inside one governed Product document. It also required a dated snapshot label on the handoff tally so it cannot act as a second live tracker, and a post-act note where receipt wording had been overtaken. Receipt, answer, correction, independent verification and Judge acceptance are reported as separate events.
nodes.rationale: graph-coverage requires a curated node per docs/ markdown file. This node also records the Product section 7.1 intra-document contradiction as a review finding against B-087's inventory.

nodes.label: B-090: B-084 and B-087 Are Related by Routing, Not Shared Lifecycle
nodes.description: Lane B finding that separates two records. Read the entry header for current lifecycle status. B-084 owns the manual-intake specification correction, including the Product section 7.1 residual it had already named, and closes on new governed-source commit evidence plus independent verification. B-087 owns planning decisions and routing, and closes on accepted decisions plus truthful branch dispositions. Closing one cannot close the other; B-087 waits on B-084 only if J4 expressly places B-084's application inside the iteration. The general rule: copying a residual into a second canonical packet gives two records that can drift on the same correction.
nodes.rationale: graph-coverage requires a curated node per docs/ markdown file. This node also carries the routing-not-shared-lifecycle rule between a planning record and a specification-correction record.

nodes.label: B-091: J4 Planning-Only Application Boundary
nodes.description: Lane B blocked-on-decision entry that framed J4 as a two-option choice. Read the entry header for current lifecycle status. Choice A, recorded by the Judge, keeps the iteration planning-only and defers B-084's source application to its own Phase 1 unit, owner Lane A / Cowork, trigger a Judge act approving B-084's exact write set. It also established that J1-J4 each need a decision or an explicit deferral with owner and trigger - silence is not a deferral - and that graph success means equality with the final committed HEAD, not a lower bound, with no narrative commit-distance tally.
nodes.rationale: graph-coverage requires a curated node per docs/ markdown file. This node also records the silence-is-not-a-deferral rule and the equality criterion for graph currency.

nodes.label: B-092: B-087 Closure Evidence Sequence
nodes.description: Lane B finding that set a finite closure order for B-087. Read the entry header for current lifecycle status. Verified requires evidence at an existing committed revision, so every handoff answer and resolution commit lands first, one exact path per commit under D-184; the untracked Graphify synchronization runs once, last, against the resulting HEAD; and no tracked status edit follows that sync - the ordering that breaks the recurring stale-graph cycle. It also removed B-088 from B-087's routed branches, because an entry cannot be both a sibling and a branch.
nodes.rationale: graph-coverage requires a curated node per docs/ markdown file. This node also carries the commit-then-sync ordering rule that prevents graph drift after closure.
